newsitem.title: GERMANY: Only Lufthansa pilots approve strike authorisation.
newsitem.headline: Only Lufthansa pilots approve strike authorisation.

text.p: Germany's DAG union said on Wednesday that pilots at Lufthansa AG gave sufficient approval to a strike-authorisation ballot but that flight attendants and ground workers in the union did not.

The DAG said 87 percent of the pilots at the German airline who are union members gave their approval but that flight attendants and ground personnel did not reach the required 70 percent level to give authorisation for a potential strike.
The DAG, saying the results did not rule out a strike, said it would discuss the results of the balloting on Friday at a meeting in Hamburg and review its strategy.

The union did not say when a strike might take place but again called on Lufthansa to put forward a new proposal that offers a contract of shorter duration than the current one of 27 months and a higher wage increase.
The voting results were a blow to the union, which had predicted union members would give approval to the strike vote.

But a DAG official said any strike action by pilots would severely hamper or shut down the German national flag carrier, which is struggling to cut costs ahead of full European airline industry deregulation set for April.

Lufthansa, hardening its stance against the union, said on Tuesday it would not change the pay offer that also includes a 1.8 percent wage increase in 1998 and a one-time payment of one-third of a month's salary that the DAG has rejected.
